name: Bebop JamSettlement settle() arbitrary interactions drain approvals
summary: JamSettlement.settle skipped signature checks when the caller was the order's taker and then ran every caller-supplied interaction as a call from the settlement contract. With an empty order naming itself as taker, the attacker passed token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) interactions that spent allowances users had granted the settlement contract directly, on Ethereum, Arbitrum and Base.
notes: Re-anchored from the reported Arbitrum 0xe5f8fe69 (08:35 UTC): the same attack bytecode ran on Ethereum at 06:52 UTC from 0xbc87e828. JamSettlement has the same address and code on each chain, each deployed separately; the Ethereum deployment is the anchor's target. The Base leg is the queue lead eip155:8453:0x9099383a (a different sender), and 0x4abf7df9 is an MEV bot's copy on Arbitrum.

Campaign found by listing every account with an Approval to the settlement on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain and Blast and their token transfers between 1 and 20 August 2025 sent by someone else; legs that run from a pre-deployed contract on chains not traced here may be missing.

The 0.01 WETH on Ethereum and 0.010654452660354139 WETH on Arbitrum were ERC-20 allowance pulls, as shown by the WETH Transfer logs in the anchor and 0x4abf7df9; they are recorded under their token addresses.
